description: The line plot illustrates the performance, measured as Accuracy@1 (%), of two large vision-language models—GPT-4o and Claude-3—across different tree widths, defined as the maximum number of child nodes per node in a search tree. The x-axis, labeled “Maximum Number of Child Nodes (Tree Width),” ranges from 1 to 5 with integer tick marks at each unit. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy@1 (%)”, spans from 20 to 35, with major gridlines and tick labels every 5 percentage points. The GPT-4o model is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers; its accuracy starts at 24.4% at tree width 1, rises sharply to 28.9% at width 2, peaks at 34.4% at width 4, and then slightly declines to 31.1% at width 5. The Claude-3 model is shown with a dashed light blue line and ‘x’ markers; it begins at 26.7% at width 1, increases to 27.8% at width 2, then gradually decreases to 24.4% at width 4 and further to 20.0% at width 5. The plot suggests that GPT-4o benefits more from increased tree width, especially between widths 2 and 4, while Claude-3’s performance peaks early and declines steadily thereafter.
